detail: Quantified, not yet modelled. 0.0007 units a round on a 1-8 Hi-Lo ramp, because rounds are sparser after the low-card runs that push the count up. Worse on an unbalanced count: 18% high on a six-deck KO ramp keyed on the pivot, because a KO count reaches its pivot late in the shoe where rounds are thinnest.
doneWhen: The frequency model weights rounds rather than card positions, most likely a Markov chain over running count and depth whose step is one round, and matches the simulator's histogram within its noise without reweighting.
title: Cut-card effect
